01

Can you catch sturgeon in the Fraser River?

“Fraser River” is not enough detail for a licence purchase. Ask the guide to name the reach and confirm whether the trip crosses a tidal boundary. A catch-and-release plan still needs the appropriate licence and must comply with closures.

The provincial sturgeon plan requires a basic freshwater licence plus the White Sturgeon Conservation Licence upstream of the tidal zone. DFO manages tidal sport-fishing rules. Check the exact water, date and licence conditions before you leave.[1] [2]

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

Planned waterFirst checkDo not assume
Non-tidal FraserFreshwater licence plus White Sturgeon Conservation Licence.A basic freshwater licence alone covers sturgeon.

A route through bothAsk which licences and restrictions cover each part.A guide’s boat crosses only one jurisdiction.
02

What are the Fraser River sturgeon catch-and-release rules?

Use a single barbless hook and plan a quick, in-water release. B.C.’s guideline defines a large sturgeon as 1.5 metres or longer: never lift it from the water. Do not use ropes or tailers, tow it by the tail, or drag it onto a bank or dock.

Have the camera ready and keep any photo brief. The guidance says to recover the fish nose-first into the current and release it when it struggles to swim. Let the guide manage the fish; do not enter deep or fast water to improve a photograph.[3]

  • ✓Agree on the release location before the first bait goes out.
  • ✓Keep large sturgeon in the water.
  • ✓Keep hands away from gills and gill plates.
  • ✓Make space for the person who removes the hook.
  • ✓Skip the photo if it delays the release.
03

What tackle should the guide supply?

The provincial guideline calls for heavy rods and reels, single barbless hooks, and line rated at least 130 lb. DFO also specifies a single barbless hook for tidal Fraser catch-and-release sturgeon fishing. Ask the guide to supply a complete outfit suited to the intended reach.

Check the whole system rather than buying one heavy rod. Ask how the crew handles a hooked fish, clears the other lines and moves to the release area. Ask who manages the anchor and boat. Those jobs need a plan before the rod bends.[3] [2]

04

How do two release plans compare?

This table is a trip-planning exercise, not a list of available guides. Use it to compare the answers you receive. A clear release procedure matters more than a promise about fish size.

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

Plan offeredQuestion to resolveYour next step
Boat trip with an in-water release areaWho controls the boat and fish during the release?Ask for the procedure before departure.
High dock or steep bankCan a fish stay in the water throughout release?Choose another location if the release needs a lift.
Photo on a beachWill the fish remain supported by water?Do not accept a plan that drags a large fish ashore.
Tidal and non-tidal stopsWhich licence covers each reach?Resolve both parts before buying the trip.
05

What is the best month to catch sturgeon?

Choose your river reach before choosing a month. Seasonal opportunities and closures differ along the Fraser, so check the rules for your exact date and location. An advertised year-round trip does not mean every reach is open. Ask the guide to explain the current restrictions before you book.

For a first visit, choose a date with room to change the plan. Ask when river and weather conditions are assessed, when the guide contacts you, and what happens if the outing cannot proceed. Keep that answer with the meeting address.[1] [2]

07

What should you ask before paying for a trip?

  • ✓Name the river reach and applicable licences.
  • ✓Confirm the full dock-to-dock duration and meeting point.
  • ✓Ask about seating, toilet access and physical demands.
  • ✓Confirm all tackle, bait, release tools and safety equipment.
  • ✓Ask whether tagging is planned and who is authorized to do it.
  • ✓Get weather cancellation and rescheduling terms in writing.

A few good questions

Before you head out

Can you keep a Fraser River sturgeon?

No. DFO states that sturgeon cannot be retained from tidal or fresh waters in British Columbia.

Do you need a licence for catch and release?

Yes. Choose the licence for the exact water. Non-tidal sturgeon fishing requires both the basic freshwater licence and White Sturgeon Conservation Licence.

Can you lift a large sturgeon for a photo?

B.C.’s guideline says not to lift large sturgeon, defined as 1.5 metres or longer, from the water. Plan a quick in-water photo.

Can you use a barbed hook?

Use a single barbless hook. Both the provincial sturgeon guideline and DFO’s tidal Fraser rule specify this.

Does a guide trip include a licence?

Ask the operator. A tackle package is not proof of personal licence coverage. Resolve the licence requirements before the trip.

Is a high dock suitable for sturgeon fishing?

The provincial guideline says elevated docks are unsuitable for landing sturgeon. Choose a location where the fish can remain in the water.
